Bug_Title: EC: equals(…) used to compare incompatible arrays (EC_INCOMPATIBLE_ARRAY_COMPARE)
Bug_Details:
This method invokes the .equals(Object o) to compare two arrays, but the arrays
of incompatible types (e.g., String[] and StringBuffer[], or String[] and int[]).
They will never be equal. In addition, when equals(...) is used to compare arrays it
only checks to see if they are the same array, and ignores the contents of the arrays.
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates the bug by using .equals() to compare two arrays of incompatible types: a String[] and an int[]. Using .equals() in this manner only checks for reference equality, not for actual content equality, and due to incompatible types, they will never be equal.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test case triggers the bug by passing a String[] and an int[] to the showBug method. This leads to a comparison using .equals() between incompatible types, which will never be equal and incorrectly returns false when the test expects true.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that the test passed successfully, as shown by 'OK (1 test)'. This suggests that the bug was not triggered during the test execution.
